title: Govt warns TV channels over Programme Code violations, urges caution in AI use
excerpt: New Delhi, October 21 (IANS) The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (I&B) on Wednesday advised private satellite television channels to strictly comply with the Programme Code and exercise caution while using artificial intelligence tools in news and programme production, warning that violations could attract regulatory action. In an advisory, the ministry said several channels had violated provisions of the Programme Code prescribed under the Cable Television Networks (Regulation) Act, 1995, and the Cable Television Networks Rules, 1994. It cautioned that any breach of the code could invite action under the existing regulatory framework."The use of AI tools may be limited to assistive capacity without compromising the accuracy, authenticity or sensitivity of news content," it said. The ministry also raised concerns over the growing use of artificial intelligence technologies in broadcasting and asked channels to exercise due caution while deploying AI tools, including generative AI, for graphics, virtual news presentations and other programming. According to the advisory, AI may be used only in an assistive capacity and should not compromise the accuracy, authenticity or sensitivity of news content. Broadcasters were reminded of their responsibility to maintain editorial standards and ensure that technology does not distort factual reporting. The ministry said an inter-departmental committee had observed that telecasts on various channels were not in conformity with the spirit of the Programme Code. The committee noted instances where similar news reports and visuals on comparable topics were aired across multiple channels in a manner that raised concerns regarding compliance with broadcasting norms. The committee recommended strict adherence to statutory provisions and stressed that inappropriate behaviour, objectionable language or undesirable conduct should not be normalised through television broadcasts. The advisory also called upon channels to carefully select and sensitise panellists participating in debates and discussion programmes to prevent the dissemination of communal, inflammatory or anti-national content. Broadcasters were asked to use safeguards such as muting, warnings, disclaimers or discontinuation of feeds whenever necessary to prevent derogatory, abusive or provocative remarks from being aired.

title: Dy CM Sanghavi meets top Japanese executives to boost investment and jobs in Gujarat
excerpt: Gujarat is in talks with Japanese companies for fresh investments in semiconductors, data centres, automobiles and specialised manufacturing, with 24 suppliers linked to Suzuki Motor Corporation expressing interest in setting up operations in the state on a fast-track basis. Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi, who is leading a state government delegation to Japan, held two roundtable meetings involving 129 Japanese companies in Tokyo on Wednesday. The discussions included a proposed investment of more than Rs 4,500 crore by Furukawa Electric in optical fibre cable manufacturing for data centres, a new specialised chemicals unit by Sumitomo Chemical in Bhavnagar and expansion plans by Honda that could create 4,000 jobs by the end of 2027 or early 2028. At a luncheon roundtable at Hotel Imperial in Tokyo, Sanghavi met 57 industrialists from various sectors to discuss investment opportunities in Gujarat. A separate meeting brought together 72 companies from Suzuki's automobile supply chain, of which 24 expressed interest in establishing operations near Suzuki's manufacturing plant at Hansalpur. The discussions come as Suzuki's annual car production in Gujarat has reached 10 lakh units and is expected to double to 20 lakh units in the coming years. Sanghavi also met Toshihiro Suzuki, President of Suzuki Motor Corporation, to discuss the company's operations and future plans in the state. Among the major proposals discussed was Furukawa Electric's planned investment of more than Rs 4,500 crore in optical fibre cable manufacturing for data centres. The company is in the final round of discussions for the project, which would mark the first time it manufactures this product outside Japan. Sumitomo Chemical has decided to establish a specialised chemicals unit for the semiconductor sector in Bhavnagar, while Tokyo Electron is in the final round of discussions on a semiconductor-related project in Gujarat. Kyowa Leather has agreed to set up a plant to manufacture polyurethane (PU) leather in the state, with the location expected to be finalised within a month. Honda's expansion plan, meanwhile, is expected to generate 4,000 new jobs in Gujarat by the end of 2027 or early 2028. During the visit, Sanghavi also held meetings with Japanese Foreign Affairs State Minister Nakasone Yasutaka and Iwate Prefecture Governor Takuya Tasso. He met representatives of 11 other major companies, including Sumitomo Chemical, Furukawa Electric, Honda, Tokyo Electron, Kyowa Leather, JERA, MUFG Bank, Marubeni, Sanrio, Meiraku and Moririn. The delegation presented Gujarat as an investment destination, highlighting the availability of industrial land, port infrastructure, power supply and approvals for new projects. The proposed investments in optical fibre cables and semiconductor-related manufacturing are expected to support industries linked to data centres and artificial intelligence, alongside the expansion of the state's automobile supply chain."When Japanese leaders think of India, they think of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The warmth and trust he built with Japan, from his days as Gujarat Chief Minister to his deep friendship with the late Prime Minister Shinzo Abe, has made state Japan's first choice in India," Sanghavi said."Today, that trust is turning into factories, investment and jobs for Gujarat's youth, under the leadership of Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel," he added.

title: Google introduces new Gemini tools for small businesses
excerpt: Google has announced new Gemini tools for small business owners, including a dedicated business landing page, brand asset creation, financial analysis and integrations with Google and third-party applications. The new business landing page will allow users to access tools for brand development, financial analysis and customer insights from a single interface. Gemini will also connect with Google Business Profile, Google Ads and Google Workspace, as well as third-party applications including Adobe, Canva, Dropbox, Shopify, Wix, Zoho and Xero. Tools for marketing and financial analysis The new tools will allow businesses to upload their websites, brand kits, fonts and colour palettes to define their visual identity in Gemini. Using Google's Nano Banana 2.1 image generation model, users can create visual assets for product launches and marketing campaigns. Gemini will retain the specified visual style for subsequent requests. Gemini will also analyse spreadsheets, receipts and purchase records to generate financial visualisations and interactive models, allowing business owners to review financial data. Small businesses using Gemini Google highlighted several small business owners who use Gemini for business operations. In Maharashtra, farmer and content creator Santosh Jadhav used Gemini to assess soil suitability, estimate seed requirements and prepare an investment budget for ginger farming. He also documents his use of technology in agriculture through online content. In Bordeaux, France, ceramicist Morgane uses Gemini to write product descriptions, newsletters and social media content for her business, Bleu Clémentine. The company claims the tool saves her two to three hours a day. In Jakarta, Indonesia, Gumilang used Gemini to develop branding, merchandise and partnership proposals for Barelz Arena, a sports and entertainment venue he established in a space beneath railway tracks. In Goiânia, Brazil, personal organiser Patricia Morais uses Gemini for customer service and content creation. She also uses Google Business Profile to build her business's local visibility. Google said the business landing page, marketing and finance tools, and new app integrations would begin rolling out globally to Gemini app users in the coming days. The company also offers Gemini for businesses seeking AI tools with centralised administrative controls, data governance and enterprise security features.
